sections.title: Oral
sections.heading: Taken by mouth, as a pill.
sections.body: SELFTAC® degraders are designed to be small enough to be swallowed, not injected.

sections.title: Gut
sections.label: In the gut
sections.heading: The dimer comes apart into two monomers.
sections.body: In the gut, each SELFTAC® dimer dissociates at its reversible linker into two small monomers, which are absorbed.

sections.title: Plasma
sections.label: In the bloodstream
sections.heading: Monomers and dimer, in equilibrium.
sections.body: In the plasma, two monomers keep joining into the dimer and coming apart again at the reversible linker: a dynamic equilibrium.

sections.title: Barrier
sections.label: The barrier
sections.heading: Only the monomers get through.
sections.body: The dimer is too large to penetrate the cell membrane or the blood-brain barrier. Each small monomer passes through on its own.

sections.title: Complex
sections.label: Ternary complex
sections.heading: Inside the cell, a dimer forms the ternary complex.
sections.body: Monomers and dimers are in equilibrium here too. One dimer binds the target protein and an E3 ligase: a ternary complex.

sections.title: Degraded
sections.label: Degradation
sections.heading: Tagged, then broken down.
sections.body: Ubiquitin marks the target and the proteasome destroys it. The degrader is free to find the next one.
